episode.title: Map a control-character shortcut to backward deletion in the text input handler
episode.before: At parent commit ecb388045c5d542de3b124c3fc255a78e74c2a84, the text area's key-event match handled unmodified Backspace by calling delete_backward(1), but had no branch for Control+h. Control-modified characters were excluded from the plain-character insertion branch, so a Control+h event reached the unhandled fallback and did not edit the text.
episode.after: At commit db30a6f5d86650ae7c5a3d40975c7c4e9daf98af, the text area's input handler treats Control+h as an alternative representation of unmodified Backspace and routes both events to the existing delete_backward(1) operation. Generic composer input is forwarded to this handler, so the shortcut applies to normal composer editing while retaining the existing grapheme/element-aware deletion behavior and start-of-text no-op.
episode.diff: The implementation adds one alternative KeyEvent pattern—KeyCode::Char('h') with exactly KeyModifiers::CONTROL—to the existing unmodified-Backspace match arm in codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/textarea.rs. The change is five inserted lines in one implementation file; it does not alter the deletion primitive, other shortcut mappings, call sites, or tests.

evidence_units.claim: In the parent state, plain characters accept only NONE or SHIFT modifiers, unmodified Backspace invokes delete_backward(1), and no Control+h branch exists in the inspected key-event match.
The pinned change adds a Control+h KeyEvent alternative to the existing unmodified-Backspace arm, with both representations invoking delete_backward(1).
evidence_units.source: git diff ecb388045c5d542de3b124c3fc255a78e74c2a84 db30a6f5d86650ae7c5a3d40975c7c4e9daf98af -- codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/textarea.rs, hunk at lines 229-238

evidence_units.claim: In the resulting implementation, exact Control+h and unmodified Backspace are normalized to the same backward-deletion operation; Alt+Backspace remains a separate word-deletion branch.
delete_backward(1) is a no-op at the beginning of the text; otherwise it finds the previous atomic boundary and removes the range between that boundary and the cursor.
The composer sends generic key events through handle_input_basic to TextArea::input, making the text-area mapping the behavioral integration point for ordinary composer editing.
The existing delete_backward_and_forward_edges test verifies that one backward deletion removes the preceding unit and moves the cursor, while deletion at the start is a no-op.

The pinned commit is db30a6f5d86650ae7c5a3d40975c7c4e9daf98af with parent ecb388045c5d542de3b124c3fc255a78e74c2a84; its subject identifies PR #2412 and issue #2391, and its recorded scope is five insertions in one textarea implementation file.
evidence_units.source: git show --stat --format=fuller db30a6f5d86650ae7c5a3d40975c7c4e9daf98af and issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0]

evidence_units.claim: The commit changes only codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/textarea.rs and adds no direct regression test that constructs a Control+h event, so the new event-to-operation mapping lacks a change-specific test oracle.
evidence_units.source: git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-status -r db30a6f5d86650ae7c5a3d40975c7c4e9daf98af; pinned diff inspection

candidate_atomics.name: normalize-equivalent-key-event-to-existing-edit-action
candidate_atomics.title: Route an equivalent key event to the existing edit action
candidate_atomics.description: Extend a text-input event dispatcher so an exact modifier-and-key representation of a familiar editing command shares the already established operation and semantics of the canonical key event.

semantic_action.intent: Make an alternate terminal keyboard representation perform the same observable backward deletion as the canonical Backspace event.
semantic_action.pre_state: The canonical Backspace event invokes one-unit backward deletion, but the alternate control-modified character is unmatched and therefore produces no edit.
semantic_action.post_state: Both exact event representations invoke the same existing backward-deletion primitive, while other modifier combinations and editing commands retain their prior branches.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the dispatch table to confirm both representations share one operation, then verify through the deletion primitive's unit oracle that the preceding atomic unit is removed, the cursor is updated, and deletion at the beginning remains a no-op. A direct alternate-event regression test remains absent.

candidate_workflows.name: add-conflict-bounded-editing-shortcut-alias
candidate_workflows.title: Add an exact keyboard alias for an existing text-editing command
candidate_workflows.description: Identify an unmatched key representation at the text-input dispatch boundary and map it narrowly to an existing, tested edit primitive without duplicating editing logic or broadening unrelated modifier behavior.

workflow_graph.goal: An alternate keyboard representation triggers the same text mutation and boundary behavior as an established canonical editing key.
when_to_use: A terminal or input environment emits a distinct key-and-modifier event for a familiar editing command.
The input dispatcher already owns a tested primitive with the required editing semantics.
The proposed event is currently unmatched at the relevant dispatch boundary.
anti_goals: Do not reimplement backward-deletion or cursor-boundary logic in the shortcut branch.
Do not broaden the match to additional modifier combinations that are not established as equivalent.
Do not remap unrelated navigation, word-deletion, insertion, or submission commands.
not_applicable_when: The alternate event is intercepted by a higher-level mode, popup, or global shortcut before reaching the text-input dispatcher.
The desired behavior differs from the existing canonical edit primitive.
The proposed key-and-modifier combination already has another required action in the applicable dispatch context.
inputs: The canonical key event and its existing edit operation
The alternate key code and exact modifier set
The input dispatch boundary and upstream forwarding call site
Behavioral tests for the shared edit primitive
workflow_graph.entry_state: The canonical event performs the intended edit, while the alternate representation reaches the dispatcher but has no matching edit branch.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The canonical and alternate exact events converge on the same existing edit primitive, preserving its cursor, boundary, and no-op behavior without changing unrelated mappings.

steps.condition: The alternate event is unmatched and semantically equivalent to the canonical event in this input context.
steps.validation: Confirm the exact alternate key/modifier pattern shares the canonical match arm, trace generic input to that dispatcher, and apply the existing deletion oracle for mutation and boundary behavior.

validation_ladder: Diff inspection: verify that only the alternate event pattern was added to the canonical command arm.
Call-site inspection: verify that ordinary composer key events reach the modified dispatcher.
Primitive unit oracle: verify one-unit backward deletion and the start-of-text no-op.
Deferred regression oracle: add or run a direct input-event test comparing the alternate event with canonical Backspace; this commit provides no such test.
stop_conditions: Stop if the alternate key combination is already assigned in the relevant input context.
Stop if upstream handling prevents the event from reaching the dispatcher.
Stop if equivalence requires changing the underlying edit primitive or unrelated command behavior.
Do not claim complete shortcut regression coverage without a direct event-level test.
unresolved_or_deferred: No direct test constructs Control+h and asserts equivalence with Backspace.
The evidence bundle lacks PR reviews, status checks, discussion, and issue body, so repository-wide conflict analysis beyond the inspected dispatch path is unavailable.
No test execution result is present in the pinned commit or supplied bundle.

unresolved_questions: Was a direct Control+h event regression test executed outside the committed test suite? The available checkout and GitHub bundle do not provide that result.
Did platform-specific terminal testing confirm that all intended environments emit KeyCode::Char('h') with exactly KeyModifiers::CONTROL? The supplied evidence does not record such validation.
